item.text: {"search_note":"I found no direct 2024 evidence about Kishida handling prisoners of war, battlefield targeting choices, or operational proportionality decisions, because Japan was not conducting the relevant military operations. The available record is mainly policy-level humanitarian and legal language, which limits how far the judgment can go. Best reading: yes on respect for civilian protection and humanitarian law in stated policy; no direct evidence of battlefield violations or prisoner-abuse decisions.","evidence":[{"title":"Summit on Peace in Ukraine (Summary)","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"June 15, 2024","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html","summary":"Kishida said peace in Ukraine must be “just and lasting,” grounded in the UN Charter and international law, and must not justify unilateral changes by force or coercion. He also said Japan would contribute to nuclear safety, electricity, and mine action. It also rejected attacks on civilians and threats to shipping.
